questions.question: Before starting a trip, you should:

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.
Remove the relay valves.
Close the emergency line valve.

questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the rear emergency and service line valves to check for air leaks. Listen for escaping air. Then close both valves before you drive.

questions.question: A tractor protection valve:

options.text: Keeps air in a brake system if there is a bad leak.
Prevents a truck from being stolen.
Prevents a trailer from being accidentally released.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in a brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. It closes automatically when air pressure gets too low.

questions.question: Which action will NOT help prevent a rig from rolling over?

options.text: Keeping the cargo as close to the ground as possible
Driving slowly around turns
Driving on the shoulder of a road

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving on the shoulder of a road
questions.explanation: To prevent rollover, keep cargo weight low and drive slowly around turns. Driving on the road shoulder does not help prevent rollover.

questions.question: If the emergency air line loses pressure:

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System will activate.
The service air line will activate.
The emergency brakes will activate.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If air pressure is lost in this line, the emergency trailer brakes will activate.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should apply the brakes:

options.text: In the same way as you would in a vehicle without ABS.
As the vehicle is placed in neutral.
With the hand brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the same way as you would in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Apply brakes in a vehicle with ABS the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: When traveling under 40 mph, maintain a following distance of at least ____ for every 10 feet of your vehicle.

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds

questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake and connects to the ____ valves.

options.text: Relay
Supply
Emergency

questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor without a semi-trailer
A tractor with two semi-trailers
A tractor that travels faster than the speed limit

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. These are difficult to operate and require caution.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Often have taller trailers than single commercial vehicles.
Are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more driving skill than single commercial vehicles. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on a downgrade.
Should never be used for parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve for parking. It may release air pressure and cause the brakes to release. Instead, use the parking brake or wheel chocks.

questions.question: What happens when you push in the trailer air supply control?

options.text: Air goes to the trailer.
The air brakes turn off.
The vehicle will not skid.

questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull out the control to stop the air supply and apply the emergency brakes.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.
Assume the trailer has ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure if a trailer has ABS, look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes.

questions.question: After connecting the air lines to the trailer during coupling, what should you do next?

options.text: Send air to the trailer.
Apply the emergency brake.
Disconnect the glad hands.

questions.explanation: When coupling a trailer, the steps you follow are important for safe operation. After connecting the air lines to the trailer, you should send air to the trailer.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It lets the wheels lock up.
It stops the wheels from locking up.
It makes the vehicle easier to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) helps prevent the wheels from locking up when you brake hard. When ABS detects that the wheels are about to lock, it reduces the braking pressure to a safe level.

questions.question: Trailers built before ____ do not need spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When you park a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from rolling.

questions.question: What happens if an air supply control is in the "emergency" position?

options.text: The vehicle will speed up.
The trailer emergency brakes will engage.
More air will go to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will engage.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have air supply controls with levers instead of knobs. When an air supply control is set to "emergency," the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes engage.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor without a trailer
A tractor attached to two trailers
A tractor with a tank

questions.explanation: A tractor without a semi-trailer is called a bobtail tractor. Drivers must be careful when operating a bobtail tractor.

questions.question: When testing ____, slowly move the vehicle forward and use the hand brake control.

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System
The emergency braking system
The trailer service brakes

questions.explanation: To test the trailer service brakes, make sure the air pressure is normal and the parking brake is released. Then move the vehicle forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control. The brakes are working if you feel them engage.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
A valve that shows the fuel level
A valve that limits the cargo amount

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve is also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar. It controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while moving could cause a skid.

questions.question: Why do combination vehicles need extra space on the road?

options.text: They drive slower than other commercial vehicles.
They weigh more than other commercial vehicles.
They need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space on the road because they are longer and need more distance to turn and stop. Managing space properly is important when operating a combination vehicle.
